title: GraphQL-to-SQL AST Compiler & Query Optimizer with LATERAL Joins
problem: GraphQL APIs built with traditional ORM resolver models suffer from the devastating N+1 query problem, triggering hundreds of sequential database queries to fulfill a single nested API request. Application-level caching and DataLoaders patch the symptom but fail to optimize database execution plans. This project builds a production-grade GraphQL-to-SQL compiler in TypeScript and Node.js. The compiler traverses GraphQL abstract syntax trees (ASTs), maps selection sets to relational schemas, infers table relationships, and transpiles deeply nested GraphQL queries into a single, highly-optimized SQL query utilizing PostgreSQL JOINs and LATERAL subqueries with parameterized prepared statements.
use_cases: High-performance backend database gateways eliminating N+1 database queries at the compiler level
Data-intensive enterprise analytics APIs serving deeply nested relational data in a single database round-trip
Open-source ORM and GraphQL engine internals optimizing query execution pipelines
hard_parts: Traversing arbitrary GraphQL AST selection sets and generating corresponding relational SQL JOIN and LATERAL expressions
Resolving complex nested pagination (e.g. first: 5, offset: 10) inside SQL LATERAL subqueries without multiplying result sets
Parameterizing all user filter arguments securely to guarantee complete SQL injection immunity
Calculating static query complexity scores during compilation to reject computationally abusive queries
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating AST visitors, schema mappers, SQL expression builders, and complexity guards
Automated compiler test suite verifying that a 4-level nested query compiles into exactly 1 parameterized SQL query
Anti-fake verification script submitting dynamic nested queries and asserting exact single-statement SQL generation

components.name: GraphQL AST Visitor & Schema Mapper
components.purpose: Traverses GraphQL query ASTs, validates selections against schema metadata, and builds intermediate IR trees

components.name: SQL Join & LATERAL Expression Generator
components.purpose: Transpiles intermediate representation trees into unified SQL SELECT statements using JOIN and LATERAL subqueries

components.name: Parameterized Predicate & Pagination Transpiler
components.purpose: Transforms GraphQL where filters and pagination arguments into parameterized SQL clauses ($1, $2)

components.name: Query Complexity Analyzer & Guard
components.purpose: Computes static query cost based on field depth and multipliers, rejecting queries exceeding safety budgets

architecture.data_flow: Incoming GraphQL query strings enter the compiler; the GraphQL parser generates an AST; the Complexity Analyzer calculates static query depth and multiplier costs, terminating execution if safety thresholds are breached; the AST Visitor traverses selection sets, mapping fields to relational table columns; the Join Generator constructs a single unified SQL query using LATERAL subqueries for one-to-many relationships; all filter values extract into parameterized arrays; the final single SQL statement dispatches to PostgreSQL in exactly one database round-trip.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Static complexity thresholds rejecting queries exceeding maximum cost budgets; strict parameterization preventing SQL injection.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a GraphQL-to-SQL compiler in TypeScript that transpiles nested queries into a single SQL statement using LATERAL subqueries.
worksheet.q2: Target users: database engineers, compiler developers, and backend platform architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: high-performance database gateways, analytics APIs, and ORM internals.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: AST selection set traversal, LATERAL subquery generation, parameterized filter extraction, and static query complexity scoring.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 8-table relational schema with 40 columns and 50 benchmark queries. Synthetic schemas only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: SQLite dialect mode.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Cartesian product explosion. Fallback: JSON-aggregated LATERAL subqueries.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static SQL strings. Anti-fake check 5 constructs dynamic aliased query at runtime and asserts alias appears in generated LATERAL SQL.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local relational schema transpilation only.
